title: GENEROSITY
mv: But to do good and to communicate forget not: for with such sacrifices God is well pleased.
mvp: “But to do good and to communicate forget not: for with such sacrifices God is well pleased.” Hebrews 13:16
assignment: State five (5) practical ways you can be generous without giving money. (2X5=10 marks).

b.x: Generosity is an aspect of God's character. It is an attractive quality we need to cultivate as God’s children. The opposite of generosity is selfishness, self-centeredness, greed and self-importance. Generosity goes beyond giving money; it also includes offering our time, talents, and resources to meet the needs of others. Generosity has many biblical sources and is related to kindness and goodness, a fruit of the Holy Spirit (Galatians 5:22-23; Proverbs 22:9).

i: God is generous: God, in His unfathomable love, gave humanity His most precious gift, His Son Jesus Christ, for our redemption. It is expedient that we demonstrate this nature (John 3:16; Romans 5:7-8).
A proof of love: Sharing our substance with others is a practical proof of our love for them (1 John 3:17-18).
It enlarges God’s kingdom: Generosity fuels evangelism, missions and church growth (Acts 2:44-47). Like the Philippians, we must constantly support Kingdom projects (Philippians 4:15-17).
It produces blessings: A cheerful giver never lacks (Proverbs 11:25; 2 Corinthians 9:6-8).

Generosity is all-encompassing: Giving flows from a heart that is always willing to share. It includes offering our time, talents, and resources to meet the needs of others (Galatians 6:2, 1Thessalonians 5:14).

b.x: To grow a generous heart, believers must:

i: Be Selfless: As believers, we must not be selfish (Philippians 2:3).
Give Cheerfully: Giving cheerfully is proof of a generous heart (2 Corinthians 9:7).
Remember the Source: We must remember that God is our source and the one who makes it possible to get all that we have (1 Corinthians 4:7; James 1:17).
Be Compassionate and Empathetic: Find out what is missing and go all out to meet the need (2 Kings 4:11-17). Leave everyone better than you met them (Luke 10:33-35).
Listen to the Holy Spirit: Do not ignore, argue or doubt what the Spirit of God is leading you to do (Acts 10:9-16). Be sensitive to obey.
